transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, doctor. I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently. I've also been eating very little, sometimes just a bite or two of food a day.
Do you find that you are restricting your food intake because you feel an intense fear of gaining weight or because you feel that your body shape or weight is unacceptable?

Yes, exactly. I restrict my food so strictly because I am absolutely terrified of gaining even a single pound. When I look in the mirror, I just feel so fat and unacceptable, and honestly, my entire self-worth depends on keeping my weight down.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of intense fear of weight gain, restriction of food intake, and distorted body image where self-worth is tied to weight is highly specific to Anorexia Nervosa. Major Depressive Disorder remains a common comorbidity, but the diagnostic criteria for Anorexia Nervosa are now clearly met, allowing for a narrowing of the list.
